summary: Request: canonical audit manifest, SIEM bridge consistency check, and AML evidence scope
description:
Issue summary: Northbridge Trust requires an evidence bundle to satisfy an AML/financial regulator request. They want a reproducible export manifest that ties delivered SIEM batches to the canonical audit ledger (per-transaction checksums), plus scope guidance for AML-related fields and a signed delivery proof.

Impact: Customer cannot complete their regulator questionnaire. They are pausing onboarding of a new payments product until evidence is accepted. Business impact: potential go-live delay and legal exposure for missed evidence deadline.

Environment: prod tenant for Northbridge Trust, eu-west region. SIEM forwarder: customer-managed SFTP endpoint (sftp://sftp.northbridge-trust.local), payload format: compressed JSON lines, daily batches, per-batch HMAC-SHA256 header expected.

Requested deliverables: canonical manifest schema (field-level mapping to our audit model), per-batch checksum/HMAC verification instructions, sample signed delivery (Rsa-SHA256 signature of manifest), cover letter for regulator describing retention windows and redaction rules, and a short Q&A mapping AML fields (transaction_id, user_id, entity_type, amount, risk_score, alert_id) to exported columns.

Steps to reproduce / verify: 1) Generate a sample daily export for tenant 9482 for 2026-03-10. 2) Produce manifest.json with batch checksums and resume token. 3) Sign manifest with our signing key and deliver to customer SFTP. 4) Provide verification script (python) that re-computes HMAC and verifies signature.

Attachments: customer questionnaire PDF (attached by customer in initial email), SFTP host fingerprint provided by customer, sample transaction IDs for verification.

Notes: Customer explicitly asked for non-repudiation proof (signed manifest), and guidance on which fields are considered PII vs AML-relevant so they can include appropriate redaction justification in their submission.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:14 - Asha Patel (Support): Received initial request from Northbridge Trust. Captured questionnaire, SFTP host key, and ask for signed manifest + HMAC verification script. Marking P1 due to regulator deadline. SLA for first response set to 2026-03-13.

2026-03-12 11:02 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Acknowledged. Will validate export pipeline and signing key access. Tentative plan: produce sample manifest within 24 hours and schedule SFTP push to their test endpoint. Need to confirm which signing key to use (prod-signing-v2 or escrow key).

2026-03-12 15:30 - Northbridge Trust (Customer): Provided additional sample transaction IDs and clarified regulator expects per-record sequence numbers and a human-readable field map in CSV format. Asked whether we can include a reversible pseudonymization example for 'user_email' field.

2026-03-13 08:45 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Confirmed we can produce manifest signed with prod-signing-v2. Asked Security team for reversible pseudonymization guidance — flagged to Security for approval. Created temporary SFTP test account for delivery and shared creds via secure channel.

2026-03-13 14:10 - Security (internal comment, via ticket): Reversible pseudonymization requires HSM-backed KEK split; cannot provide reversible mapping in evidence. Recommended documenting that pseudonymization is irreversible by default and offering a redaction + mapping exemplar that uses a salted HMAC (non-reversible) plus a controlled enrollment process as alternative.

2026-03-14 09:00 - Asha Patel (Support): Shared draft manifest + sample delivery with customer and included verification script. Customer requested small change to CSV field order. Asked SRE to regenerate signed manifest with amended field map.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12: Pulled last 7 daily export batches for tenant 9482 from /exports/9482/ (s3://redwood-exports/eu-west/9482/). Verified per-batch checksum header exists for three recent batches; two older batches missing checksum due to exporter version 1.9 fallback. Hypothesis: customer previously used an older exporter that didn't emit per-record sequence numbers consistently.

2026-03-12: Checked signing key availability: prod-signing-v2 present in KMS alias 'arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456:key/prod-signing-v2', IAM role 'exporter-service' has decrypt/sign permissions. Ran test signature creation on sample manifest and validated with public key. Link to test output: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/exports/manifests?from=now-2d&to=now

2026-03-13: Validated SFTP connectivity to customer's test endpoint (host key matched). Performed dry-run upload of sample_manifest_v1.json.sig. Observed successful 226 Transfer complete. Logged SFTP session ID: sftp-session-9812.

2026-03-13: Security reviewed reversible pseudonymization and advised against including reversible mapping. Proposed alternative: include field 'user_email_hash' with HMAC-SHA256(salt+email) and document salt rotation policy.
resolution: 2026-03-14: Delivered verified artifact bundle to customer's test SFTP and to their legal contact via secure transfer. Bundle contents: sample_export_2026-03-10.jsonl.gz, manifest_2026-03-10.json, manifest_2026-03-10.json.sig (RSA-SHA256 signature), verification_script.py (python 3.11), field_map.csv (customer-requested order), and a short cover_letter_aml.txt describing retention and redaction policies.
Verification: Customer ran verification_script.py against the delivered manifest and confirmed HMAC and signature verification succeeded. Customer confirmed field order change applied.

Follow-ups: 1) Create an internal KB article summarizing reversible pseudonymization policy and recommended exemplar (KB-exports-pseudonymization-2026). 2) Engineering to schedule rollout of exporter v2.0 to backfill missing per-record sequence numbers for historical batches (linked: SUP-720145). 3) Legal to review the cover letter and add regulator-specific language if requested (assigned to Legal team).
Ticket state: Awaiting customer confirmation for production cutover delivery (Waiting on Customer). Will reopen if further clarifications required.
